description: E-commerce practice site: browse and search products, add to cart, register an account, place an order.
_VERIFICATION_STATUS: STARTER INVENTORY, NOT YET VERIFIED AGAINST THE LIVE DOM (created 31 Jul 2026). Every selector below is role= or text= derived from text observed on the actual pages, so the NAMES are real - but none has been confirmed to resolve to exactly one element. Before trusting it run `python -m scripts.verify_locators --only-problems` and fix whatever it reports. Then crawl a fuller draft with `python -m scripts.generate_inventory` and merge in the elements this file does not cover: the second signup form, product detail, checkout and payment are all missing.

_inventory_conventions.selectors: Every selector maps to a first-class Playwright locator: [name='x'] / #id (css), role=button[name='Save'] (getByRole), label=X (getByLabel), placeholder=..., alt=..., title=..., text=... . XPath is never emitted. An iframe-chained selector uses ' >>> '. label=/alt=/title= need page.get_by_label/get_by_alt_text/get_by_title - they are NOT page.locator() engine syntax; role= and text= work with page.locator().
_inventory_conventions.selector_strategy: This app is server-rendered with semantic HTML and readable button/link text, so role= and text= selectors are preferred over CSS: they survive restyling and read like the page. Where the crawl finds a data-qa attribute, prefer that.
_inventory_conventions.shared_navigation: Present on every page. Top navigation, so it lives once here rather than repeated on each page.
_inventory_conventions.test_owned_data: An account's cart, addresses and orders are private to it, so assertions on them are safe. The PRODUCT CATALOGUE is shared and read-only - 34 fixed products - so a named product is safe to assert on, but never assert a total that the site owner could change.

test_users.registered: A pre-registered account used for login scenarios. No privilege levels exist in this app.

common_errors.invalid_login: Your email or password is incorrect!

elements_notes._shared: Present on every page. Top navigation, so it lives once here rather than repeated on each page.
elements_notes.logout_link: Present ONLY while logged in, which makes its presence a reliable readiness signal for 'am I authenticated'. Use is_visible() on it rather than parsing the URL.
elements_notes.logged_in_as: Reads 'Logged in as <name>'. A substring match, so assert containment rather than equality.
elements_notes.delete_account_link: Permanently removes the account and shows 'ACCOUNT DELETED!'. A test that registers an account should call this at the end - there is no admin cleanup on this site and abandoned accounts accumulate forever.

elements_notes.subscribe_button: UNVERIFIED id, taken from the site's own documented test cases rather than from the DOM. Confirm with verify_locators before relying on it.
elements_notes.subscribe_success: Rendered in place after subscribing - there is no navigation and no toast.

elements.login_error: text=Your email or password is incorrect!

elements_notes._two_forms: THIS PAGE CARRIES TWO INDEPENDENT FORMS - 'Login to your account' and 'New User Signup!' - and BOTH have an email field. A selector loose enough to match 'the email input' matches both and is a strict-mode violation. Always use the form-specific key.
elements_notes.login_email_input: UNVERIFIED data-qa value. This app is widely documented as using data-qa attributes, but the exact values here were not read from the DOM. verify_locators will confirm or reject each one in seconds.
elements_notes.signup_button: Submitting this does NOT create the account - it navigates to a second, fuller form at /signup. The account exists only after THAT form is submitted.
elements_notes.login_error: Rendered as text on the same page. No redirect, no toast.

errors.invalid_login: Your email or password is incorrect!

elements.added_modal: text=Your product has been added to cart.

products.multi_match_note: Keys whose selector matches SEVERAL elements. Read them with get_all_texts / get_count / get_nth_text; never click, fill, wait on or assert against them - Playwright is strict and raises 'resolved to N elements'. Enforced by validators/method_resolution_validator.py at generation time.

elements_notes.add_to_cart_buttons: MULTI-MATCH, and worse than it looks: every product card renders its Add to cart control TWICE (once in the card, once in the hover overlay), so this matches 68 elements on the all-products page, not 34. Never click it directly - scope to one product's card, or open the product via its View Product link.
elements_notes.product_names: MULTI-MATCH and also doubled per card for the same reason. Use get_all_texts() to assert a product IS present rather than indexing into it.
elements_notes.view_product_links: MULTI-MATCH, but each href carries the product id (/product_details/<id>), which makes it the reliable way to reach ONE product.
elements_notes.added_modal: Adding to cart opens a MODAL rather than navigating. It blocks the page underneath, so a scenario adding two products must dismiss it between them or the second click fails with 'intercepts pointer events'.
elements_notes.search_input: UNVERIFIED id, from the site's documented test cases rather than the DOM. Search matches on product NAME and submits to the same page.
elements_notes._empty_search: A search matching nothing renders NO result cards rather than an empty-state message. Assert absence by counting cards, not by looking for text.

cart.multi_match_note: Keys whose selector matches SEVERAL elements. Read them with get_all_texts / get_count / get_nth_text; never click, fill, wait on or assert against them.

elements_notes._test_owned: The cart belongs to this test's own session or account, so asserting an EXACT row count is safe here - unlike the shared catalogue.
elements_notes.cart_rows: MULTI-MATCH. Narrow to the product the test added rather than assuming a row index.
elements_notes.cart_table: UNVERIFIED id, from the site's documented test cases rather than the DOM.
elements_notes.proceed_to_checkout_button: Proceeding while logged out shows a Register/Login prompt instead of the address form, so a checkout scenario must authenticate first.
